agenda_items.description:
Notices and meeting information are attached to the agenda and minutes, including: availability of simultaneous interpretation and accessibility accommodations; in camera meeting procedures; information items not subject to discussion; personal information disclaimer for correspondents and public speakers; notices regarding minutes; and hybrid participation details.
Accessible formats and communication supports are available, upon request.
Except where otherwise indicated, reports requiring Council consideration will be presented to Council on January 28, 2026 in Built Heritage Committee Report 27A.
The deadline to register by phone to speak, or submit written comments or visual presentations is 4 pm on Monday, December 8, 2025, and the deadline to register by email to speak is 8:30 am on Tuesday, December 9, 2025.

sub_agendas_items.title: Application for Demolition at 208 Slater Street, a property designated under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act as part of the Bank Street Heritage Conservation District
sub_agendas_items.description:
File No. ACS2025-PDB-RHU-0040 - Somerset (14)
This report will be submitted to Ottawa City Council on December 10, 2025.
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
At the outset, the Committee received a detailed slide presentation overview of the report from Ms Taylor Quibell, Planner II, Planning, Development and Building Services (PBDS) Department.  A copy of this presentation is held on file with the Office of the City Clerk. 
Ms Marcia Wallace, General Manager, Planning, Development and Building Services (PBDS) Department, Mr. Court Curry, Director, Rights-of-Way, Heritage and Urban Design Services, PDBS and Ms Megan Brodie, Associate Legal Counsel, Legal Services Department, were also present to respond to questions.
The Committee then heard from the following delegations:
At the conclusion of questions to the delegations and to staff, and with Committee discussions having concluded, the report recommendations were put before Committee and were ‘Carried’, as presented, on a division of six ‘Yeas’ to three ‘Nays’, as outlined below:
For (6):         Members C. Legault and B. Bourns, and Councillors A. Troster, J. Leiper, Vice-Chair S. Plante and Chair R. King
Against (3):   Members C. Quinn and J. Maddigan and Councillor C. Kelly

sub_agendas_items.title: Conservation Design Guidelines - 284 King Edward Avenue

sub_agendas_items.title: Designation of 300 Rochester Street under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Ms Linda Hoad, Heritage Advocacy Committee, Heritage Ottawa, had registered to speak but opted not to do so when asked by the Chair whether she would need to speak if Committee were prepared to ‘Carry’ the item on consent. 
She also submitted written correspondence on behalf of Heritage Ottawa dated 7 December 2025.  A copy of this submission is held on file with the Office of the City Clerk.

motions.motion_text:
Report Recommendation(s)
That the Built Heritage Committee recommend that Council issue a Notice of Intention to Designate 300 Rochester Street under Part IV of theOntario Heritage Actaccording to the Statement of Cultural Heritage Value attached as Document 5.

sub_agendas_items.title: Nomination of the ByWard Market as a National Historic Site in Honour of its 200th Anniversary
sub_agendas_items.description:
File No. ACS2025-PDB-RHU-0061 - Rideau-Vanier (12)
This report will be submitted to Ottawa City Council on December 10, 2025.
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Mr. Court Curry, Director, Rights-of-Way, Heritage and Urban Design Services Heritage and Urban Design Services, Planning, Development and Building Services (PDBS) Department, introduced this item, following which, the Committee received a detailed slide presentation overview of the report from Ms. MacKenzie Kimm, Planner III, PDBS.  A copy of this presentation is held on file with the City Clerk.
The Committee then heard from Ms Jillian Stewart (The Properties Group), speaking on behalf of herself and of Ms Samantha Sigler, representing a group of commercial landlords in the ByWard Market. 
Written correspondence was received from Ms Linda Hoad, Heritage Ottawa Advocacy Committee, Heritage Ottawa, and is held on file with the Office of the City Clerk.
At the conclusion of questions to staff and to the delegation, and with Committee discussions having concluded, the report recommendations were put before Committee and were ‘Carried’, as presented.
